review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Round monetary results with the project's round_money helper
item.description: Any money value returned from a calculation must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
item.content: Before returning a computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money (half-up to the cent). Check the money module for existing helpers like to_money/ZERO and reuse them for consistency with invoice_total and line_total.

item.title: Read the money module and existing sibling functions before implementing
item.description: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py and existing functions (line_total, invoice_total) reveals the required rounding and conversion conventions.
item.content: When adding a money-related function, first cat the money module and neighboring functions in the same file. Mirror their patterns (to_money on inputs, round_money on outputs, ZERO as sum seed) rather than inventing new arithmetic.

item.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly
item.description: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero or the invoice has no lines.
item.content: Compute the denominator first; if it is falsy, return ZERO (the project's zero constant) instead of dividing. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement and avoids ZeroDivisionError.
